articles.title: Bold College Fantasy Football Predictions for Week 9
articles.summary: College fantasy football analysts Eric Froton and Nick Bromberg get bold for Week 9.
articles.body:
Yahoo Sports College Football analysts Eric Froton and Nick Bromberg reveal their boldest predictions for Week 9 of the CFF season.

Nolan James Jr. runs for 100+ yards and a score

While Aneyas Williams was considered the opening day starting running back for the Irish, his inability to grind out yardage on the interior opened the door for challengers. James has shown the ability to consistently create extra yardage, averaging 3.64 yards after contact while Williams is at 2.29 YAC with a disappointing 4.32 yards per carry.

James fully took over the room versus BYU last week, rushing 16 times for 77 yards while scoring 10+ fantasy points in all seven games this season. I think James clears the century mark with a score this weekend against Navy and emphatically lays claim to the starting job for the rest of the season. — Froton

Missouri QB Austin Simmons throws for 300+ yards, 3 TDs against Arkansas

The Tigers took their lumps in a 31-3 loss to Ole Miss last game, but they've been a steamroller against the rest of their schedule, scoring at least 24+ points in their other six games while ranking 15th nationally with 24% of completions gaining 20+ yards. Simmons has competently led this aggressive passing attack that averages 10.5 of target depth per pass (11th) and 16.3 yards per successful dropback (24th).

He has the advantage of facing a beleaguered Arkansas defense that is still finding its footing under new HC Ryan Silverfield, ranking 126th in yards per successful dropback and 109th in yards per drive. I think Missouri gets back on track in style, as Simmons leads the way with 300+ yards and 3+ touchdowns. — Froton

The Duke RB has been one of the most productive running backs in college fantasy football thanks to his touchdown production. He's scored 13 TDs and has found the end zone in every game.

However, he hasn't cracked the 100-yard rushing mark since he had nine carries for 116 yards against William & Mary in Week 4. He's made up for that with his receiving ability — Sheppard had 91 receiving yards against Georgia Tech and then 11 catches for 98 yards against North Carolina — but is in line to finally cross the century mark again on Saturday. Boston College is allowing over 150 rushing yards per game. — Bromberg

Pitt's Cataurus Hicks will continue to thrive despite QB uncertainty

Pitt's season has gone south ever since QB Mason Heintschel suffered a season-ending knee injury against Virginia Tech. But the Panthers' subsequent struggles at quarterback — and on offense in general — haven't deterred Hicks' fantasy relevance.

Hicks has scored at least 19 points in three of the last four weeks. He had five catches for 149 yards and a score last week against Miami after grabbing five passes for 135 yards and a TD the week before against Boston College. And Georgia Tech, Hicks' next opponent, is all out of sorts this year.

Hicks is available in over 70% of leagues. There are far worse options available if you're in need of a receiver. — Bromberg

articles.title: "He’s always gone above and beyond": Lewis Hamilton's special gesture for Kim Kardashian's kids played a major role in their romance
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton may be known for his seven Formula One world titles, but a thoughtful gesture away from the racetrack reportedly helped him win Kim
articles.body: Lewis Hamilton may be known for his seven Formula One world titles, but a thoughtful gesture away from the racetrack reportedly helped him win Kim Kardashian's heart. The British racing star is said to have made a strong impression on the reality star by showing genuine care for her four children. His decision to gift them a dog, named Halo, reportedly became one of the moments that strengthened their relationship. Hamilton has also spoken openly about enjoying his time with Kim's children, offering a glimpse into their growing family bond.Lewis Hamilton's gift to Kim Kardashian's children reportedly won her heartAccording to a source cited by PEOPLE, Hamilton's relationship with Kardashian grew stronger because of the attention he gave her family from the beginning. The seven-time world champion reportedly understood that her children were an important part of her life and made an effort to build a connection with them.The insider said: “Gifting Kim’s kids a dog is just one of the thoughtful things Lewis has done for them.”They added: “A big reason Kim fell in love with him was because of how caring and considerate he was with her kids right from the start. He’s always gone above and beyond for them.”The source also claimed that Kardashian feels fortunate to have Hamilton in her life, describing him as a supportive partner who makes her happy.The couple's new pet, Halo, has already become part of their family. Kardashian gave fans a glimpse of the golden retriever in a July 30 Instagram post, while Hamilton shared a photograph of the dog on September 22.Lewis Hamilton opens up about spending time with Kim Kardashian's childrenHamilton has also offered a rare glimpse into his relationship with Kardashian's family. Speaking during a press panel ahead of the United States Grand Prix in Austin on October 25, the driver discussed how much he enjoys spending time with the children.“My girlfriend’s kids, I love spending time with them,” he said.“She’s got four, so I’m getting to play with these kids.”He also confirmed that he was behind the family's latest addition, saying: “I got them a dog this year, so little Halo is a new member of that family.”Kardashian shares four children with her former husband Kanye West: North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm. Hamilton's comments suggest that he has embraced spending time with the family rather than keeping his relationship separate from her responsibilities as a mother.Meanwhile, Kardashian recently offered another glimpse into her feelings on The Kardashians. She revealed that Hamilton matched all 55 qualities on her partner wish list and admitted she was “really, really happy” with him.She added: “To just look up one day and be like, ‘Wait, let me check the manifest list,’ and be like, ‘Yes! Yes! Yes!’ It’s a crazy feeling.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “It’s not always a bed of roses": Andre Agassi opens up about marital struggles as Steffi Graf's influence on his life emerges
articles.summary: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have built a marriage that has lasted through fame, personal struggles and the pressures of professional sport.
articles.body: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have built a marriage that has lasted through fame, personal struggles and the pressures of professional sport. When the tennis legends celebrated their 24th wedding anniversary in October 2025, their relationship drew renewed attention. Behind their long-standing bond, however, lies a story of difficult moments, emotional challenges and the steady support that helped them stay together. Agassi has often credited his wife with bringing stability to his life, while people close to the couple have described their relationship as strong but far from perfect.Andre Agassi credited Steffi Graf for changing his lifeLast year, Agassi marked their anniversary with a heartfelt message on social media, writing, “24 years with this wonderful woman. Happy Anniversary Steffi, you are my unicorn!”According to a source quoted by Heat, Graf played a significant role in helping Agassi maintain the stability he needed after overcoming his past struggles with substance use. The insider said Agassi had already stopped using drugs before their relationship began in 1999, but credited his wife with helping him remain on track.“Without Steffi by his side things could have turned out very differently for Andre, everyone that knows him would agree that she’s been a great influence on his life.”The couple married in a private ceremony, choosing jeans and bare feet instead of a traditional wedding celebration. They welcomed their son Jaden shortly afterwards and later had their daughter Jaz.Despite their sporting achievements, the couple chose to raise their children away from the pressure of professional tennis. Their son pursued baseball, while their daughter developed interests in dance and horseback riding.Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf's marriage faced its share of strugglesTheir relationship has not been without disagreements. The same insider told Heat that the tennis legends experience arguments and difficult periods like other couples.“It’s not always a bed of roses, they’re still human,” the source said.The insider added that Agassi sometimes struggles with his emotions, while Graf's calm personality helps keep their family grounded.Away from the spotlight, the couple have built a quiet life in Las Vegas. Both reportedly prefer spending time at home with their children and a small circle of friends rather than attending celebrity events.Interestingly, their home does not display their Grand Slam trophies. Graf once revealed, “We only have our children's trophies. Jaden from baseball and Jaz from hip-hop dancing.”As their children grow older, the former champions have found more time for their shared interests. They still play tennis together for fun, while Agassi has also embraced pickleball and made his professional debut in 2025.Their marriage may have faced difficult moments, but their shared values, family life and mutual support have remained central to their relationship.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “I try to show up": Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle opens up about handling the emotional pressure of his demanding NHL career
articles.summary: Connor McDavid, the Edmonton Oilers’ star player and captain, has remained focused on the team’s performance as they are off to a strong start in the
articles.body: Connor McDavid, the Edmonton Oilers’ star player and captain, has remained focused on the team’s performance as they are off to a strong start in the 2026–27 NHL season under new head coach Mike Babcock sitting at the top of the Pacific Division with a 9–2–2 record (20 points) through 13 games. Amid this, Connor McDavid’s wife, popular entrepreneur Lauren Kyle has opened up about her life.Connor McDavid’s wife, Lauren Kyle, reflects on how difficult it has been for her to control her emotions amid his stressful career on the iceIn an appearance on the Powerful Ladies podcast, Connor McDavid’s wife, Lauren Kyle, has admitted how difficult it has been for her to handle the Edmonton Oilers’ captain’s stressful life and her work.The host of the podcast asked her, “How do you stay calm because you have so much going on that we're about to dive into. That's all your stuff. Yeah. You're so accomplished. You have so much going on. Then you also have to hold space for a huge career that your husband also has. Like how do you balance all the stress you have plus whatever stress he's bringing into your space too?”To this, Connor McDavid’s wife, Lauren Kyle said, “Yeah, it's definitely tough. I think that. In general, like the games bring, especially in the finals, against a team that, we lost against last year and we were hoping to have redemption this year. It was hard to compose myself in those moments. The next day I was supposed to go on the podcast and I was emotionally drained and mentally drained.”The popular entrepreneur added, “So it's definitely definitely hard. I can't say it's easy. I think for me, I always just try to focus on my own businesses and like staying present for those things in my life because it gives me a distraction and allows me to, ground myself a little bit in those moments.”Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle continued, “And I do know that I need to show up for Connor in a way in order to be strong for him. Like I can't have all of the emotions because he needs someone who has some strengths and composure. At least in front of him. I definitely sometimes don't have composure when I'm not around him, but definitely in front of him. I try to show up in a way that, provides him with support too.”Connor McDavid has always praised Lauren Kyle for being thereConnor McDavid and his wife, Lauren Kyle, have been together since 2015 even though the two recently tied the knot in 2024.In many of his interviews, the Edmonton Oilers’ captain Connor McDavid has reflected on how Lauren Kyle stood by his side through all the difficult days.For now, all eyes remain on Connor McDavid as he gears up to face the New York Rangers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Could Bryce Underwood Have a Future at Michigan Playing a Different Position?
articles.summary: With Tommy Carr taking over at quarterback and Bryce Underwood's future under center suddenly uncertain, could Michigan find another way to utilize the forme...
articles.body:
When Bryce Underwood arrived at Michigan , the expectation was that he would become the next great Wolverine quarterback. Now, less than a full season into the Kyle Whittingham era, it's fair to wonder whether his future in Ann Arbor might involve playing an entirely different position.

It sounds crazy considering Underwood's recruiting pedigree, but it's at least a conversation worth having.

Underwood was benched at halftime against Penn State after completing just five of 11 passes for 43 yards and two interceptions. True freshman Tommy Carr replaced him, led Michigan to a 21-18 victory and subsequently earned the starting assignment against Indiana.

Suddenly, Underwood's path back onto the field looks considerably more complicated, and maybe even impossible.

But here's the thing: Underwood is still one of the most physically gifted athletes on Michigan's roster.

At 6-4 and roughly 230 pounds, Underwood possesses a rare combination of size, speed and explosiveness. Even when he's struggled throwing the football, his ability to make defenders miss and generate yards with his legs has been obvious.

So why not find another way to get him involved?

The most intriguing possibility would be some sort of hybrid offensive role. Underwood could line up in the backfield alongside Carr, take direct snaps in short-yardage situations or even operate as a running threat on designed packages. Coincidentally, Whittingham's old program, Utah, is utilizing a two-QB system to perfection this year.

Essentially, Michigan could use him as an offensive weapon without asking him to shoulder the responsibilities of a traditional quarterback.

There's also the possibility of experimenting with Underwood at wide receiver or tight end, although those transitions would be considerably more complicated. Being a tremendous athlete doesn't automatically translate to running precise routes, catching passes in traffic or understanding blocking assignments. Underwood has been a pass catcher sparingly during his high school 7-on-7 days, but playing one of those positions at a place like Michigan in the Big Ten is a completely different animal.

And then there's the biggest obstacle of all: Would Underwood even entertain the idea?

He came to Michigan to play quarterback as THE No. 1 signal caller in the nation, and changing positions would represent a massive departure from the expectations surrounding his arrival. With the transfer portal providing opportunities elsewhere, there's no guarantee he'd be interested in reinventing himself.

It's also important to remember that Underwood is still quite young. Struggling as a quarterback early in his career doesn't mean he can't eventually develop into an excellent one. After all, his physical gifts are off the charts and it still feels like he could be unleashed with some different parameters.

Michigan shouldn't abandon that possibility simply because Carr has provided a spark.

Still, Whittingham and offensive coordinator Jason Beck desperately need more explosive playmakers, and Underwood's abilities are difficult to ignore.

Nobody is suggesting Michigan has actually approached Underwood about changing positions. But if Carr establishes himself as the long-term answer at quarterback, the Wolverines could eventually face an interesting decision.

Do they leave one of their most talented athletes standing on the sideline, or get creative enough to put him on the field?

It's an unconventional idea, but given Michigan's offensive struggles, perhaps it's one worth exploring.

articles.title: Joey Logano losing touch of his fourth Cup championship in 2026
articles.summary: Joey Logano is losing touch of a potential fourth NASCAR Cup Series championship after Talladega Superspeedway in 2026.
articles.body:
Joey Logano's pursuit of another NASCAR Cup Series championship suffered a significant setback during Sunday's YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. The Team Penske driver started 16th, led 23 laps and won Stage 2 before a violent accident ended his afternoon in 34th place.

Logano displayed competitive speed throughout the second half of the event, repeatedly exchanging the lead with Ricky Stenhouse Jr. during the closing stages. His strongest moment came in Stage 2 when he narrowly defeated Kyle Larson for the stage victory by just 0.012 seconds.

However, his afternoon ended dramatically on Lap 183 when contact from Carson Hocevar destabilized his Ford in the outside drafting lane. Logano spun into traffic, and his car overturned during the ensuing 15-car accident.

The No. 22 Ford came to rest upside down before safety crews returned it to its wheels, allowing Logano to exit. The damage prevented him from continuing, leaving him 34th after 183 laps.

Logano earned 15 points and climbed one position to fifth in the Chase standings with 2,341 points. However, he now trails championship leader Kyle Larson by 100 points. Logano remains mathematically eligible for the title but will need substantial gains during the final two races.

articles.title: Young RBs fuel Sheridan in revenge win vs. Tri-Valley
articles.summary: Sheridan's young running backs carried a heavy load in a Division III, Region 11 playoff clash with Tri-Valley.
articles.body:
Sheridan pulls away from Philo, stays atop MVL-Big, top photos

THORNVILLE — Sophomore S.J. Shriner and freshman Emmitt Gilder have shined in Sheridan's backfield in Logan Russell's absence.

Their efforts were vital again on Friday night at Paul Culver Jr. Stadium, combining for more than 280 yards as a senior-laden offensive line paved the way in the sixth-seeded Generals' 38-35 triumph against No. 11-seed Tri-Valley in the Division III, Region 11 playoffs.

Shriner scored three times, including on a 9-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter, while Gilder had game-sealing runs of 28 and 25 yards in the closing minutes of the final stanza. Sheridan remained unbeaten at home in playoff games.

The Generals (11-0) ended a five-game losing streak to the Scotties and avenged a 38-21 loss to them in Week 9 of the regular season. They travel to third seed Columbus East (9-1) in the quarterfinals at 7 p.m. on Nov. 6; that winner plays either No. 2 seed Licking Valley or No. 7 Granville in the semifinals.

Sheridan coach Paul Culver III praised his young running backs, while complimenting his five seniors on the offensive line, especially Milo Bullock.

"We told Milo we were going to run behind him on that final drive, and he led the way," Culver III said. "Our line did the job all night. Those two ran hard behind them, and Emmit could have scored late, but he had the intelligence to go down so we could take a knee and seal it.

"This win is for the 26 seniors, who mean so much to me, this community and school and to each other," he added. "I've been through a lot the past few weeks, and they've carried me. We talked about standing in the gap coming into this game, and they did that. They deserve this win."

Sheridan led 17-14 at the half on Liam Gutridge's 28-yard field goal right before the half.

The Generals took control in the third. Carson Harris scored on a 17-yard run to open the second-half scoring. After TJ Connors intercepted Tri-Valley's Stone Spiker on the ensuing possession, Logan Russell converted the takeaway into points with a 4-yard burst, making it 31-14 with three minutes left in the third.

However, the Scotties did not go quietly.

Leevi Wade, who ran for a school-record 362 yards in their regular season meeeting, capped the ensuing Tri-Valley drive with a 2-yard TD dive. After forcing a Sheridan punt, Spiker found top receiver Lucca Gargasz for a 79-yard scoring strike, which pulled the Scotties within 31-28 with 10 minutes left in the game.

Sheridan extended its lead on the next drive, as Shriner weaved 10 yards to the end zone, while Tri-Valley came back, as Spiker hit Logan Clapper for a 4-yard TD with four minutes left.

Despite Tri-Valley's rally falling short, coach Austin Jones never lost faith in his squad.

"They have super talented running backs and they're good up front," Jones said. "We also missed some tackles on the boundary. People doubted us coming into the season, and we could have packed it in at 3-3. But, our guys strapped it up and went to work to reach this point. Our seniors laid a good foundation for this program, and I know it's not easy after a game like this, but I'm proud what this group accomplished."

Shriner finished with 173 yards and three touchdowns, including scoring runs of 15 and 10 yards in the first quarter. Gilder added 108 yards on nine totes, and Tyce Whiteman was 10-of-16 passing for 111 yards with 38 yards on five carries for Sheridan.

Wade was held to 93 yards on 21 carries with three scores, including first-half TD runs of 1 yard in the first quarter and 2 yards in the second, and Spiker went 12-of-15 through the air for 209 yards to go with 42 yards on four rushes.

"Tri-Valley changed their identity, and hats off to their coaches for making that change so quickly," Culver III said. "That forced us to raise the bar. Our defensive coaches put in a great game plan and made good adjustments. I'm proud that our guys responded, and we get another week together."
authors: Brandon Hannahs, Special to the Zanesville Times-Recorder

articles.title: Thunder’s Injury Nightmare Could Have a Silver Lining for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder watched as injuries piled up, turning an encouraging start into a difficult stretch for a team with championship expectations. Befo...
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder watched as injuries piled up, turning an encouraging start into a difficult stretch for a team with championship expectations. Before discussing standings or individual awards, the priority remains the players facing recovery and the teammates processing what happened.

Jalen Williams suffered a fractured left fibula and dislocated left ankle against the Los Angeles Clippers. Cason Wallace sustained a torn labrum in his left shoulder during that game. General manager Sam Presti announced that both players would require surgery, with return timelines to be determined afterward.

Jaylin Williams also exited that game with right wrist soreness, although he was subsequently cleared to play against Phoenix. That distinction matters. His situation should not be grouped with the extended absences facing Jalen Williams and Wallace.

For Oklahoma City, replacing their contributions will require more than shifting minutes around. Losing a secondary creator and a perimeter defender changes how the Thunder can attack opponents, protect leads and distribute responsibility throughout games.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Faces a Different Challenge

The weight now falls more heavily on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, even with Oklahoma City needing contributions throughout its roster. The two-time MVP already commands defensive attention. Without Williams beside him, opponents have another reason to load up against his drives and force somebody else to create.

That could mean more scoring opportunities, but it also means tougher possessions. Additional shots do not automatically produce better basketball. Gilgeous-Alexander will need to balance aggression with trusting teammates, particularly when defenses try to turn every trip into a difficult individual assignment.

This is where his leadership becomes just as important as his production. Oklahoma City needs its best player to provide stability while others adjust to responsibilities they might not have anticipated carrying so early.

Another MVP Case Would Have to Be Earned

Before these injuries, a third consecutive MVP might have felt difficult to imagine. Voter fatigue can become part of the conversation when somebody keeps winning, and another excellent season might struggle to feel different from the previous two.

However, there is an argument available if Gilgeous-Alexander meets this challenge.

If he keeps Oklahoma City among the Western Conference's elite while increasing his production, voters would have a different situation to evaluate. Maintaining that standard without key teammates would provide evidence of his value beyond the numbers themselves.

That is a major if. The Thunder still need reliable shooting, defensive execution and enough contributions around him to win consistently. A scoring increase attached to a slide down the standings would make a less convincing argument.

Efficiency matters, too. Bigger numbers would carry more weight if Gilgeous-Alexander produces them without sacrificing the decision-making that makes him so effective.

Nobody should describe his teammates' injuries as good fortune. Their health comes first, and Oklahoma City's championship hopes are stronger with them available.

But if Gilgeous-Alexander helps hold this team together, keeps it competing near the top of the West and elevates his own play, dismissing another MVP case simply because he already has two would become difficult to justify.

articles.title: No one can stop Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo on tough and-1 vs. Pacers
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo continues to exert brute force with an incredible highlight during the Miami Heat’s NBA Cup matchup against the Los Angeles Lakers on F...
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo continues to exert brute force with an incredible highlight during the Miami Heat's NBA Cup matchup against the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night.

Antetokounmpo started the 14th season of his NBA career, his first with the Heat. Following a remarkable tenure with the Milwaukee Bucks, the franchise sent him to Miami as the superstar forward looks to compete for his second championship.

Miami got off to a slow start, losing its first four games. They have since bounced back with back-to-back wins over the Atlanta Hawks and the Pacers, finally gaining traction with their expectations as a squad.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Antetokounmpo balled out in his latest performance in Miami's blowout win over Indiana. One specific highlight among many occurred in the early minutes of the second half. He was inside the paint as he actively secured multiple offensive rebounds , boxing out Indiana players as much as possible before finally getting the shot to go and count the foul he drew.

How Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat played against Pacers

Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat finally gave home fans their first win, routing the Pacers by a 145-125 score in the NBA Cup group stage.

Six players scored in double-digits for Miami in the win, including Antetokounmpo. He led the squad with a stat line of 31 points, 18 rebounds, 10 assists, and one block. He shot 13-of-19 from the field, including 1-of-2 from beyond the arc, and 4-of-6 from the free-throw line. Bam Adebayo came next with 27 points and nine rebounds, Klay Thompson had 25 points and three assists, while Pelle Larsson put up 18 points and three rebounds. Meanwhile, Davion Mitchell provided 15 points and 11 assists.

Miami improved to a 2-4 record this season, sitting at 10th place in the Eastern Conference standings. They are above the Indiana Pacers and the New York Knicks while trailing the Orlando Magic and the Washington Wizards.

The Heat will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Los Angeles Lakers as tip-off commences on Nov. 2 at 10 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Tyler Reddick on brink of elimination at Martinsville in 2026
articles.summary: Tyler Reddick is on the brink of elimination going into the NASCAR Cup Series race at Martinsville Speedway in 2026.
articles.body:
Tyler Reddick suffered a major setback to his NASCAR Cup Series championship hopes during Sunday's YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. The 23XI Racing driver started 33rd and ultimately finished 37th after being collected in the massive accident on Lap 132.

Reddick entered the event with momentum after winning the previous race at Phoenix Raceway. That victory had reduced his championship deficit to 56 points behind Kyle Larson with three races remaining.

However, the unpredictable nature of superspeedway racing quickly changed his situation. Reddick was among the drivers involved in the 12-car accident triggered when Ryan Blaney lost momentum in the outside drafting lane.

The damage forced the No. 45 Toyota to the garage and effectively ended Reddick's opportunity to score meaningful points. He ultimately completed 137 laps and finished 37th, collecting just one point. The result left Reddick seventh in the NASCAR Cup Series Chase standings with 2,315 points.

However, his deficit to Larson expanded dramatically from 56 to 126 points. Reddick remains mathematically eligible for the championship, but his chances have been severely diminished. He will need outstanding performances at Martinsville and Homestead-Miami, along with significant problems for Larson, to overcome the deficit.

articles.title: Reagan bounces back from disappointing loss with rout of Roosevelt
articles.summary: Ayden Fernandez and Jericko Espinosa had strong performances on the ground, and the Rattlers put on a clinic on special teams in the win over the Rough Rider...
articles.body:
Sophomore kicker Jacoby Hartofelis lined up to kick a field goal to give Reagan another positive play heading into the locker room, but the ball ended up in senior tight end Russell Reed's hands for something even better.

With four seconds left until halftime, Hartofelis was set for a 28-yard field goal attempt. A bad snap still ended up in holder and senior linebacker Nate Ramos' hands, and he quickly leaped into the air and tossed the ball to Reed for an 11-yard touchdown.

Reagan demonstrated some unexpected creativity on offense to defeat Roosevelt 52-0 Friday night at Comalander Stadium in the penultimate game of the regular season.

"They executed it, but that's not really what we intended," Reagan coach Preston Meyer said of the unexpected score.

Reagan came out firing on all cylinders against Roosevelt, a week after taking a tough 50-7 loss to rival Johnson.

"It shows how much we can face adversity and how much adversity helps a team like us," Reagan senior two-way athlete Ayden Fernandez said of getting back into the win column.

The Rattlers got on the board with a 32-yard rushing touchdown by junior running back Jericko Espinosa in a quick two-minute, five-play drive. Fernandez, Reagan's leading rusher, punched in his first score of the night on an 8-yard rushing touchdown with 7:27 remaining in the second quarter. He recorded his second score of the night with a 31-yard rush to open the scoring in the third quarter.

"We looked very clean," Fernandez said of Reagan's offense. "No mistakes."

Even Reagan's special teams got in on the scoring action before the break. Senior defensive back Landon Herrera returned a punt for a 80-yard touchdown with 3:38 left in the second quarter, minutes before the field goal unit stole their own touchdown.

Senior defensive lineman Colt Galan recovered a loose ball on Roosevelt's 5-yard line in the third quarter after the Rough Riders tried to punt it away. Espinosa quickly ran the ball into the end zone on the ensuing play for a quick score.

"I can't say enough about our kids," Meyer said. "We had a tough one last week, and they came back ready to go to work this week, and we came out and got it done."

Reagan junior kicker Dylan Sage extended the Rattlers' lead with a 37-yard field goal to start the final quarter. Senior running back Alexander Tritch scored Reagan's final touchdown of the night on a 6-yard run with 5:48 to play.

Looking ahead, Reagan is in line for a second-place finish in District 28-6A and has a spot in the playoffs locked up.

"We're going to try and go execute the best we can and get ready to get a good one in the playoffs," Meyer said.

Fernandez hopes the Rattlers will use their final regular season game as a tune up. Reagan takes on Clark next Thursday at Farris Stadium to close out the regular season, while Roosevelt faces Churchill next Friday at Heroes Stadium.

"We've got to play a really clean game," Fernandez said. "Because in playoffs, no mistakes or you lose."

articles.title: Pakistan vs Sri Lanka ODI Tri-Series final prediction, lineups and Gaddafi Stadium pitch report — who will win?
articles.summary: Read our Pakistan vs Sri Lanka ODI Tri-Series final prediction with probable lineups, team news and the Gaddafi Stadium pitch report
articles.body:
Pakistan have the bowlers and Sri Lanka have the batters, and on Saturday in Lahore one of them has to give way. The ODI Tri-Series final at the Gaddafi Stadium starts at 1.30pm IST, four days after Sri Lanka bowled Pakistan out for 110 and won by eight wickets with 31.5 overs to spare.

Pakistan had already booked their place in the final by winning their first three game. Sri Lanka still walk in with a slight edge in confidence, and a batting lineup nobody fancies bowling at.

Pakistan vs. Sri Lanka prediction: who will win?

Pakistan's attack has been the best of the three teams over the past fortnight. Shaheen Shah Afridi, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf offer plenty of variety, and with Arafat Minhas and Shadab Khan in support they defended 305 against these opponents in the opener and held England to 241. The trouble is at the other end. Their top three are all short of runs, and when the lower-middle order has to rescue them, as it did not on Tuesday, the innings can fall apart fast.

Sri Lanka have no such worry. They have passed 330 twice in the tournament and chased 430 against England. Pavan Rathnayake has 350 runs at an average of 116.67, with two hundreds against England and a 79 against Pakistan in the opener. Sri Lanka have also won six of their eight ODIs in Lahore, while Pakistan lead the overall head to head 97 to 59 across 161 matches.

Pakistan can win this if their pacemakers take early wickets, as they did in the opener. Over a whole innings, though, Sri Lanka's batting looks the more reliable side of the contest.

articles.title: Carson Hocevar eliminated from Cup championship contention in 2026
articles.summary: Carson Hocevar has been eliminated from contention in the Chase for the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series championship.
articles.body:
Carson Hocevar overcame significant adversity to finish sixth in Sunday's YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. The Spire Motorsports driver started 26th and remained competitive despite involvement in the massive accident that sent Joey Logano upside down with five scheduled laps remaining.

Hocevar, who won the spring race at Talladega, was pushing Logano in the outside lane when contact destabilized the No. 22 Ford. The resulting accident collected 15 cars and sent Hocevar's Chevrolet spinning down the frontstretch.

With four flat tires preventing him from driving back to pit road, Hocevar required assistance from a tow truck. His team subsequently repaired the car and returned him to competition without losing a lap.

That recovery proved crucial. Hocevar took advantage of the overtime finish to salvage sixth place, completing all 189 laps despite the earlier damage. The result earned Hocevar 31 points and moved him up one position in the championship standings.

Hocevar now ranks 10th in the NASCAR Cup Series Chase standings with 2,243 points. However, he trails championship leader Kyle Larson by 198 points, mathematically eliminating him from title contention. He will now focus on securing the best possible final championship position over the remaining two races.

articles.title: Ashland's comeback attempt falls short at Canal Winchester in Week 11
articles.summary: The teams combined for 80 points, opposing playmakers combined for 500-plus yards of offense, and it came down to a fourth down stop with 2.2 seconds.
articles.body:
CANAL WINCHESTER — As if Division II, Region 7 needed any further proof it's the strongest in the state, Friday's regional first-round matchup between No. 5 Canal Winchester and No. 12 Ashland was the smoking gun.

After the Arrows snuck into the playoffs as the final qualifier with a win in Week 10 with a .600 record, they were rewarded with a nearly 100-mile trip down to face the Indians. And Ashland made sure that drive was well worth it, pushing Canal Winchester to its limits in a game that featured 80 points between the teams.

In the end, it's the Indians who are moving on to Week 12 thanks to a defensive stop late in the fourth quarter in a 43-37 win.

"That team came in here ready to play and they played their heart out," Canal Winchester coach Corey Coe said. "You gotta give those guys respect because they had nothing to lose coming in here. I know what it's like to have a two-hour bus ride, and for them to come out and play like that, I give those guys a heck of a lot of credit."

Canal Winchester opened the scoring on its first possession, marching down the field with ease and capping off the drive with a 13-yard run from Jamari Snow. The Arrows responded with a Liam Hubacher-to-Killian O'Brien seven-yard connection but missed the extra point to trail by one. Ashland took the lead on a 19-yard field goal from Layton Roop, but that was short-lived as Snow punched in his second to regain the lead with 5:05 in the half.

With a little over a minute to go, before half, Kian McGhee found a wide open Rai'montez Hughley — the Ashland defensive back slipped on the turf — who went for 50 yards setting up Snow's third touchdown of the half, this time from three yards out, for a 21-9 lead at the break.

"We knew coming in that he's good," Ashland coach Scott Valentine said of Snow. "He's a guy we were going to have to tackle and he's just tough to get down. He's a physical guy and he's going to get his yardage, you just gotta try to limit it."

After mustering just nine points in the first half, Ashland exploded for four touchdowns, starting with another Hubacher-to-O'Brien strike from 30 yards out just 31 seconds into the second half. They linked up again from 16 yards out as a response to an 11-yard McGhee keeper on the Indians' first possession. Cody Noble hit a 28-yard field goal for Canal Winchester to push a 31-22 lead that the team would take to the end of the third quarter before then extending that to 37-22 on a Snow one-yard burst up the middle followed by a blocked extra point.

Hubacher called his own number from two yards out less than a minute later. Then, when the Arrows got the ball back again, he found Nevin LaRue in the end zone for the 20-yard score to make it 37-35. And Valentine trusted his quarterback again on the two-point conversion as Hubacher barreled in to tie the game with 3:41 remaining.

Another defensive lapse from the Arrows led to Sir'Anthony Washington wide open for the go-ahead 30-yard score to put the Indians on top 43-37 following another blocked punt.

With under two minutes to play, Killian O'Brien fielded the kickoff and gave the Arrows great field position to which Hubacher marched the team down to the 13. But the drive ended in an incomplete pass in the end zone on fourth down with 2.2 seconds on the clock.

"You gotta make plays one way or the other," Valentine said. "They made a couple plays, and then we had an opportunity to put ourselves in the position — that's all you can ask, right?

Just like a last season's Week 12 clash at St. Francis DeSales, the Arrows had a chance to win it late but came up short.

"It's definitely one of the toughest regions in Ohio," O'Brien said. "And I can't say I hate being part of it because I love the challenge, you get to see some dudes every year. Just two years now we fell by one score ... the opportunity was there; we just couldn't finish."

It was a night where O'Brien became the program's single-season receptions leader (95) after a 12-catch, 187-yard performance with three touchdowns and a week after he nabbed the career receiving yards record (2,746) and extended his career receiving touchdowns mark to 34.

"It means a lot ... I've worked my whole life for this, and it's one of the goals I wanted," O'Brien said. "I'm happy to see myself accomplish it, I just wish we could've got the win tonight."

"He's just an incredible player, an incredible teammate, and an incredible young man," Coe added of O'Brien. "He's really a better person than he is a football player. I'm just proud of his personal development and where he's gone since his freshman year into sophomore year, he just continues to become a better and better young man."

He also had an interception on defense and played a key role on special teams, returning kicks which set up the offense with great field position several times throughout the night.

"This is my best game now," O'Brien said. "There's three phases to the game — special teams, defense, and offense — I gotta do it all when I'm on the field."

It helped having someone on the other side of the field to feed off, too, as Snow finished the night with 35 carries for 314 yards and four touchdowns. The two playmakers combined for 501 yards and seven scores.

"He's a heck of a player and he's their guy," O'Brien said. "They rely on him to do a lot of things, and I feel like I have a lot of weight on my shoulders to do a lot of things. We just had a respectful battle back and forth ... we were hyping each other up."

The loss brings an end to what was a tumultuous season for the Arrows (6-5), who swept their nonleague opposition the first three weeks before dropping the first three games of Ohio Cardinal Conference play. But they closed out winning three of the last four to make the playoffs for the fifth consecutive season.

"Hopefully we learned some lessons," Valentine said. "When you have a young team, they've gotta grow up and they gotta do the work in the off-season. I can go back and look at things from last off-season, and some of the guys didn't think they were going to be playing as much as they ended up playing ... we just gotta get better and work harder in the offseason to get ready for next year."

Canal Winchester (8-3) now shifts its focus to four-seed New Albany (8-2) in a regional quarterfinal. It will be the second time the teams have met this season.

"They're a juggernaut," Coe said. "We were in a slugfest with them last time and ended up beating them 35-28, but I'm sure they probably left that game thinking they didn't play their best. But anytime you get to play New Albany, it's a great opportunity. Our kids are excited for it, and I know they'll be ready for the rematch at their place. This region is incredible and I'm just grateful and proud that we're still playing."

And he's now 6-0 since taking over the program after Week 5 when the Indians fell to 2-3 coming off a narrow loss to Pickerington Central.

"Canal Winchester football is my life, apart from my family," Coe said. "It's a different role I'm still learning — that universal perspective — because I'm a defensive guy and sometimes I gotta be careful about being too defensive-minded on the sideline and be more in-tune with game management. That's not an easy thing when you're still running the show on defense.

"But it's an honor and a privilege, these kids are incredible and I'm proud to be their head coach."

articles.title: Bayern Munich youth player returns after 994 days of injury misery
articles.summary: What a story of determination and resilience.
articles.body:
After nearly three years of waiting, working, and fighting to get back, Bayern Munich U-19 center-back Valentin Beckert has finally made his return.

Beckert suffered through a major ACL injury, followed by a serious hamstring injury, which might have caused him to have doubts that he would ever get back.

Well, he did it—as he returned on Monday to play five minutes against SGV Heilbronn-Freiberg.

It is the kind of moment that puts football into perspective. Behind every comeback is a player who has had to endure countless hours of rehabilitation, frustrating setbacks, and the uncertainty of wondering when the next opportunity will come.

Coming back after such a lengthy absence is an achievement in itself, regardless of what happens next. Getting back onto the pitch after 994 days is a testament to the patience, determination, and resilience required to keep pushing when the finish line feels impossibly far away.

For Beckert, the countdown is over. The focus can finally shift from recovery to football again.

Welcome back, Valentin! Here is hoping the next 994 days are filled with plenty of football, unforgettable moments, and absolutely no more time on the sidelines.
